source.title: Higher moments, extreme returns, and cross-section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with higher lagged intraday return kurtosis earn higher subsequent weekly returns, consistent with higher-moment risk and extreme-return pricing.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain top 50 contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume among assets with exact hourly/daily history for the estimation window.
feature: Excess kurtosis of causal hourly log returns pooled over W prior completed UTC days, computed from rolling raw moments. Higher signal means higher realized kurtosis.
signal_direction: Long highest-kurtosis quintile, short lowest-kurtosis quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long/short, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: Feature window ends Sunday 23:00 UTC; enter Monday open and exit next Monday open. Delayed robustness enters Tuesday open and exits next Tuesday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-minus-low weekly spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive after base costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 lookbacks positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; exclude BTC/ETH positive; exclude strongest contributor positive; one-day delayed implementation positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The paper uses intraday higher moments. This implementation uses Binance 1h log returns and a pooled rolling raw-moment estimator; market-cap weighting is unavailable, so portfolios are equal-weighted after causal liquidity screening.
